name: Constructing the Array
description: You are given an array $$$a$$$ of length $$$n$$$ consisting of zeros. You perform $$$n$$$ actions with this array: during the $$$i$$$-th action, the following sequence of operations appears: Choose the maximum by length subarray ( continuous subsegment ) consisting only of zeros, among all such segments choose the leftmost one; Let this segment be $$$[l; r]$$$. If $$$r-l+1$$$ is odd (not divisible by $$$2$$$) then assign (set) $$$a[\frac{l+r}{2}] := i$$$ (where $$$i$$$ is the number of the current action), otherwise (if $$$r-l+1$$$ is even) assign (set) $$$a[\frac{l+r-1}{2}] := i$$$. Consider the array $$$a$$$ of length $$$5$$$ (initially $$$a=[0, 0, 0, 0, 0]$$$). Then it changes as follows: Firstly, we choose the segment $$$[1; 5]$$$ and assign $$$a[3] := 1$$$, so $$$a$$$ becomes $$$[0, 0, 1, 0, 0]$$$; then we choose the segment $$$[1; 2]$$$ and assign $$$a[1] := 2$$$, so $$$a$$$ becomes $$$[2, 0, 1, 0, 0]$$$; then we choose the segment $$$[4; 5]$$$ and assign $$$a[4] := 3$$$, so $$$a$$$ becomes $$$[2, 0, 1, 3, 0]$$$; then we choose the segment $$$[2; 2]$$$ and assign $$$a[2] := 4$$$, so $$$a$$$ becomes $$$[2, 4, 1, 3, 0]$$$; and at last we choose the segment $$$[5; 5]$$$ and assign $$$a[5] := 5$$$, so $$$a$$$ becomes $$$[2, 4, 1, 3, 5]$$$. Your task is to find the array $$$a$$$ of length $$$n$$$ after performing all $$$n$$$ actions. Note that the answer exists and unique . You have to answer $$$t$$$ independent test cases.
input_specification: The first line of the input contains one integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. Then $$$t$$$ test cases follow. The only line of the test case contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the length of $$$a$$$. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$ ($$$\sum n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$).
output_specification: For each test case, print the answer — the array $$$a$$$ of length $$$n$$$ after performing $$$n$$$ actions described in the problem statement. Note that the answer exists and unique .
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1353D — Constructing the Array [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
